sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the entire trips table (495K rows) to apply the payment_type=2 filter, then hash-joins the resulting ~99K rows with the 265-row zones table, and finally groups 99K rows into 265 groups; the dominant cost is the full table scan and subsequent join on the filtered trips rows.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)
The sequential scan on trips reads all 495833 rows to find the 99167 with payment_type=2; an index on payment_type or partitioning by payment_type would avoid the full scan.

The join condition CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID adds a per-row cast overhead and may prevent join optimizations; ensuring PULocationID and LocationID share the same integer type would eliminate the cast.
The hash group by processes 99167 joined rows to produce only 265 groups; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID for payment_type=2 before the join could reduce the join input size significantly.
